screens.name: Home
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows a dominant orb, explicit touch instruction and unavailable omen across transition and settled captures; A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6.
findings: Increase the prominence of the unavailable omen's recovery guidance so the first visit offers a clearer route forward.

screens.name: Approach
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves the orb and opening message across captures, while supplied evidence reports automatic advancement and immediate advancement with reduced motion; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Verify that the brief automatic entrance does not interrupt assistive-technology focus or announcements.

screens.name: Ask — standard
screens.evidence: Sheets 01–02 show a labeled populated field, typing and voice routes, and a clear submit button, with the orb changing position between captures; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Keep the question field and submit action visually anchored during the entrance rather than allowing decorative movement to shift task content.

screens.name: Ask — 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows the enlarged question, disclosure and submit action fitting together, and supplied browser evidence reports retained context and visible submission; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Verify the same readable field and reachable submit action with a physical phone keyboard and native text enlargement.

screens.name: Listening — voice unavailable
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows consistent transition and settled layouts with typing promoted above voice retry and a persistent microphone failure notice; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Place a concise unavailable-voice explanation beside the typing action so recovery does not depend on noticing the distant bottom notice.

screens.name: Question 1 — plan readiness
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows four evenly separated choices and explicit step progress, while supplied evidence says normal answers advance immediately; A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4.
findings: Align answer wording to one readiness scale, since 'Barely started,' 'Halfway there' and 'Nearly certain' mix progress with confidence.

screens.name: Question 2 — obstacle
screens.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show stable question placement, clear step numbering and four separated responses across transition and settled captures; A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6.
findings: Provide perceivable selection confirmation before automatic advancement, including an accessible announcement.

screens.name: Question 3 — support
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 preserves the question template and shows the final step with friend, teacher, self and custom responses; A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6.
findings: Make the final answer's transition into prediction generation explicit so immediate advancement remains predictable.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows stable question context, a labeled input, Change action and disabled Continue across both captures; A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6.
findings: Add a short instruction explaining that an answer enables Continue instead of relying entirely on the muted button state.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty, 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 keeps the enlarged prompt, Change control, input and disabled Continue visible, although the prompt occupies substantial vertical space; A 7.3, F 7.3, overall 7.3.
findings: Reduce nonessential vertical spacing around the enlarged prompt to leave more room for entry when the keyboard opens.

screens.name: Custom answer — populated, 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows a readable multiline answer and fully visible reveal button, with supplied browser evidence reporting preservation after changing choices; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Confirm that the multiline field remains equally usable with native text scaling and an actual keyboard.

screens.name: Custom answer — synthetic keyboard-constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows the populated field and submit button within the constrained area but does not visibly establish full question context, which the supplied browser report says was retained; A 7.3, F 7.3, overall 7.3.
findings: Capture the focused field with its readable prompt and a physical keyboard to resolve the incomplete visual evidence of context.

screens.name: Planning — loading
screens.evidence: Sheets 09–10 show a consistent loading composition with a stage explanation, time expectation, credit reassurance and Cancel; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Verify that stage changes and cancellation results are announced without repeatedly reading the decorative loading copy.

screens.name: Research — loading
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows readable research status and cancellation while brighter mist moves behind the upper controls and orb; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Limit mist brightness behind controls so the loading atmosphere does not compete with recovery actions.

screens.name: Planning — error
screens.evidence: Sheets 05–06 show a stable error hierarchy with retry, edit and explicit no-charge reassurance, using disclosed fixture text; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Verify focus placement and error announcement when this recovery screen replaces the loading state.

screens.name: Prediction — error
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 adds Review answers to retry and edit recovery, with consistent layout but variable bright mist near the close control; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Maintain a consistently dark area behind the close control throughout the error transition.

screens.name: Planning — sensitive redirect
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–12 show support, alternative-question and edit routes plus no-spend reassurance, with the alternative-question button receiving strongest emphasis; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Give the support route stronger visual priority when the redirect says the person needs support.

screens.name: Prediction — sensitive redirect
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 repeats the sensitive recovery choices after prediction with brighter background mist and disclosed synthetic message content; A 7.3, F 7.7, overall 7.5.
findings: Emphasize the support action and reduce atmospheric competition around this more serious recovery state.

screens.name: Reveal — collapsed
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show a legible settled prediction, uncertainty label and follow-up actions, while the transition substantially dims the prediction text; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Keep essential prediction text readable during its entrance and give the several secondary actions clearer grouping.

screens.name: Reveal — expanded explanation
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows a clear expanded heading and collapse control, but the explanation begins low in the viewport beneath the full hero composition; A 7.0, F 7.7, overall 7.4.
findings: Compact the decorative header when Why expands so more explanation is immediately readable.

screens.name: Check-in
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows the outcome prompt and three responses adjacent to the result, but sharing remains the strongest action and the transition dims the result; A 7.3, F 7.3, overall 7.3.
findings: Make outcome recording the dominant check-in task and show a clear selected or saved response state.

screens.name: History — empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows a stable empty state with local-storage disclosure and a direct Ask the Ball action; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Give the empty-state action a stronger control affordance while retaining the quiet layout.

screens.name: History — populated
screens.evidence: Sheets 06–07 show a dated question and prediction with Waiting status, and supplied runtime evidence reports persistence and outcome recording; A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4.
findings: Replace the ambiguous Waiting label with a more specific check-in status and make the row's opening affordance clearer.

screens.name: History — long list
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows consistent repeated rows with the lowest visible prediction extending behind the fixed navigation area; A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4.
findings: Verify that the final row can scroll fully above the tab bar and raised orb, with no obscured action or text.

screens.name: Sky — offline samples and selected question
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows explicit offline sample disclosure, Retry, a checkmarked category and a corresponding question with a primary action; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Verify generous target areas and accessible selected-state announcements for the scattered star controls.

screens.name: Circles — offline
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 explicitly reports the offline state and shows disabled creation, Retry and restricted sharing preferences; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.5.
findings: Place the unavailable-service explanation nearer the disabled creation button and distinguish it from age-based restrictions.

screens.name: You — empty memory and settings
screens.evidence: Sheets 13 and 15 show clear plan, memory and settings sections, with the privacy row partly covered by the raised navigation orb; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Ensure the privacy row can rest fully above the raised orb and navigation surface when scrolled into view.

screens.name: Settings — keyboard focus
screens.evidence: Sheet 13 shows a strong full-row focus outline, and supplied controls evidence reports 342×52px targets, keyboard activation and persistence; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Extend this verified focus treatment to every secondary action and icon-only navigation control.

screens.name: Settings — 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 shows readable enlarged preference labels and a selected large-text switch, with content intersecting the sticky header and lower navigation boundaries; A 7.3, F 7.7, overall 7.5.
findings: Verify scroll clearance above and below enlarged settings so complete labels remain obtainable outside the sticky regions.

screens.name: Plans — standard
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 clearly labels simulated billing and selected yearly pricing, but the settled capture clips the decorative orb beneath the fixed header; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Remove or fully contain the partially clipped orb and simplify the header so plan comparison starts cleanly.

screens.name: Plans — 200% text
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 stacks enlarged plan details, retains a non-color selection checkmark and keeps the simulated continuation button visible; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Verify that pack purchases and all remaining plan terms are equally reachable at enlarged text sizes.

screens.name: Share
screens.evidence: Sheet 13 shows stable preview and format rows, while supplied runtime evidence supports PNG export and injected export-error recovery but not OS delivery; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Provide an easily enlarged preview so users can inspect the small prediction and disclaimer text before export.

screens.name: Story card
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows a coherent full-size card and clear export button across captures, with Back to sharing partly beyond the viewport; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Keep the return action fully discoverable after export and verify exported text legibility at typical story-viewing size.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: The sheets consistently establish the illustrated orb as the hero, and supplied browser evidence reports smooth rendering and stopped draws under reduced motion; A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6.
findings: Make the orb's interactive role on Home distinct from its decorative role elsewhere and avoid clipping it on Plans.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Sheets 05–15 show consistent labeled tabs and underlined active states, but the raised Ask orb overlaps content above the bar; A 7.3, F 7.7, overall 7.5.
findings: Reserve clearance for the raised orb and verify target sizes and text scaling for every small tab label.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Headers consistently pair a page title or script wordmark with a small remaining-reading balance, with larger variants shown in Sheets 01, 09 and 12; A 7.7, F 7.3, overall 7.5.
findings: Increase the small balance text's legibility and verify that changes in remaining readings are accessibly announced.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream buttons remain prominent across standard and enlarged captures, and supplied browser evidence supports submission, retry and export recovery; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Document focus and pressed states for this shared button in addition to the visible enabled and disabled states.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text actions are consistent throughout the sheets but vary from isolated links to full-width divided rows without equivalent target evidence; A 7.3, F 7.3, overall 7.3.
findings: Standardize generous target areas and visible focus treatment for Change, Cancel, Retry and other text-only actions.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Sheets 02–03 show spacious divided choices, while supplied evidence establishes immediate advancement without showing a selected choice frame; A 8.0, F 7.3, overall 7.6.
findings: Provide a perceivable selected response and accessible confirmation as the next question appears.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Sheets 01–02 show a labeled multiline field with prominent gold framing and a second lower line, and runtime evidence supports actual entry; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Simplify the double lower-edge treatment while preserving a distinct accessible focus indicator.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Sheets 01, 03 and 05 show readable enlarged multiline fields, while keyboard-context evidence is limited to a synthetic viewport; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Verify prompt visibility, caret scrolling and submit reachability with a physical keyboard at enlarged text sizes.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheets 12–13 show positional and color state changes plus a row focus outline, supported by reported 342×52px targets and Space/Enter activation; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Verify switch names, current values and state-change announcements with VoiceOver and TalkBack.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheet 08 shows a labeled free omen section whose only represented state is unavailable until tomorrow; A 7.3, F 7.0, overall 7.1.
findings: Add a successful omen capture and make the unavailable state's recovery timing more prominent.

components.name: Sky star and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 14 combines a non-color checkmark, named stars and a matching question, but does not establish star hit areas or focus order; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.7.
findings: Ensure each star has a generous labeled target and a predictable keyboard and screen-reader order.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheet 05 uses borderless sections and explicit offline messaging with disabled creation, supported by the supplied controls report; A 7.7, F 7.7, overall 7.5.
findings: Differentiate service unavailability from age-related control restrictions directly beside the affected controls.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheets 06–07 show a clear date, original question, prediction and small Waiting status but no visible selected or completed row state; A 8.0, F 7.0, overall 7.4.
findings: Clarify the row's opening action and replace Waiting with a specific, meaningful outcome or check-in status.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheet 09 shows explicit yearly selection, total and monthly-equivalent pricing, savings and a readable stacked enlarged layout; A 8.0, F 8.0, overall 8.0.
findings: Verify radio-group semantics and selection announcements while retaining the explicit simulated-billing label.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sheets 13–14 show coherent preview and full-size card compositions, although text in the small preview is difficult to inspect; A 7.7, F 7.5, overall 7.6.
findings: Offer an enlarged inspection view with accessible text equivalent to the image.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Error, voice and offline captures expose concrete recovery paths, and supplied runtime evidence reports connection and injected export-error recovery; A 8.0, F 7.7, overall 7.8.
findings: Verify alert announcements and focus recovery across each notice type, especially the bottom voice notice.

components.name: Typography system
components.evidence: The sheets consistently separate expressive serif headings from practical sans-serif controls, but utility labels and preview disclaimers are small; A 8.0, F 7.5, overall 7.7.
findings: Increase the smallest utility text and verify contrast over the brightest atmospheric frames.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: The dark gold palette is coherent, but research and reveal frames show brighter mist competing with content despite reported reduced-motion and frame-performance passes; A 7.0, F 7.0, overall 7.0.
findings: Constrain mist luminance behind text and controls while preserving the reported reduced-motion behavior.

limitations: All grades are provisional: this evaluation uses the attached screenshots and supplied runtime summary without independently executing the app or inspecting evidence files.
No screen or component qualifies for 9/10 certification because physical phone and assistive-technology checks remain unverified.
All represented settled screens and key variants are graded; matching transition captures are grouped with their settled states.
A is the normalized mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the normalized mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall uses unrounded means before rounding to one decimal.
Null denotes a genuinely inapplicable dimension; missing interaction evidence instead limits the numeric score.

Static transition frames establish composition and temporary dimming, not animation duration, focus continuity or perceptual smoothness; supplied browser motion results support only the tested browser conditions.
Partial content at viewport boundaries does not establish an unreachable action; scroll clearance, sticky-header overlap and raised-tab obstruction require direct verification.
No hard-gate failure is conclusively established by the supplied material, but physical keyboard, screen-reader and native behavior boundaries remain unresolved.
Successful live omen, populated circles, active microphone capture, populated memory editing and selected check-in outcomes are not visually represented in these sheets.
Synthetic predictions, repeated explanation text and labeled fixture messages are layout evidence only and are not scored as production-copy or model-quality failures.
Real payments, configured social backend, OS share delivery, microphone hardware, native haptics and native Dynamic Type remain unverified.
The authorized A >=9 and F >=9 threshold is not met for any screen or meaningful component.
topFixes: Resolve content clearance around the raised Ask tab, sticky headers and enlarged layouts; capture fully visible final rows and secondary actions.
Keep essential text readable through reveal transitions and reduce bright mist behind text and controls.
Show and verify selected-answer, saved-outcome and focus-transfer feedback, including assistive-technology announcements.
Verify large-text forms with physical keyboards and native text scaling, preserving the prompt, typed answer and reachable submission.
Prioritize support on sensitive redirects, outcome recording on check-in, and clearer status wording in History.
Complete physical phone and VoiceOver/TalkBack checks before considering any 9/10 certification.
